brief.headline: Aluminium rose for a fifth straight session to a three-week high, with cash up $47.50 or 1.46% to $3,303.00 and exchange stock at 245,975 tonnes - reported as the lowest since 1990 - yet the curve loosened back into a $0.50 contango on the same day, so the market bought the forward rather than scrambling for prompt metal.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. Aluminium cash settled $3,303.00 on 03-September, up $47.50 or +1.46%, and the three-month settled $3,303.50, up $50.00 or +1.54% - the fifth consecutive rising session and the highest level in more than three weeks, with an intraday print of $3,328.50 that was the best since 12-August. Because the forward rose FURTHER than the prompt, the one-day backwardation of 02-September reversed and the curve fell back through flat into a $0.50 CONTANGO. Exchange stock fell 250 tonnes to 245,975 t, which is reported as the lowest level since 1990. Aluminium led the whole board: copper cash +0.03%, nickel +0.51%, zinc -0.11%, lead -0.16%.

WHY IT MOVED, AND WHY THE CURRENCY DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT THIS TIME. The dollar index fell 0.38% and the LME euro fixing rose 0.31%, so in euro terms the same settlement still rose about 1.14% - roughly four-fifths of the move survives the currency adjustment and needs a real explanation. That is the opposite of the previous session, when a 0.17% decline shrank to 0.04% in euros and the currency accounted for essentially all of it. The public candidates for the remaining four-fifths are all inventory: a thirty-six-year low in LME stock, an eleventh consecutive weekly draw in Shanghai exchange inventory from 528,885 tonnes in mid-June to 391,498 tonnes, and Chinese ingot social inventory down another 22,000 tonnes on the week to 815,000 tonnes as seasonal restocking begins.

WHY THE CURVE IS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST GETTING CARRIED AWAY. A thirty-six-year inventory low sitting alongside a $0.50 contango is a contradiction, and the cleanest way to see it is to look sideways on the same board. Zinc's cash-to-three-month backwardation is $127.50 and it WIDENED on a session when 9,975 tonnes were delivered into warehouse - because exchange data shows one entity holds more than half the zinc warrants and cash contracts. Copper's is $84.00, down from more than $500 in mid-August. Those are curves pricing prompt scarcity. Aluminium's is not. Low registered stock and tight prompt metal are related but they are not the same thing, and only one of them is visible in aluminium today.

WHAT TO WATCH. First, whether the fifth-session rally extends or stalls at the $3,328.50 intraday high and the $3,374 level that capped the August advance. Second, whether the curve does anything at all - a contango that persists through a further inventory decline would confirm that off-warrant metal is doing the work registered stock used to do. Third, the Japanese fourth-quarter premium round, where producers have opened 18-22% below the record third-quarter benchmark and buyers are targeting below $300, which is a physical-market verdict that sits awkwardly against the inventory headline. Fourth, US August payrolls today and the central bank decision on 16-September, on which two dated public sources currently disagree about the direction of rate expectations.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE, 06:05 LONDON, BEFORE THE RING. THE BOARD ON THIS PAGE IS THE 03-SEPTEMBER-2026 OFFICIAL, and it was accepted only after a four-way verification that it passed on every leg. FIRST, the ENGLISH Westmetall overview and the cache-busted GERMAN overview carry the identical 03-September board - all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings agree line for line. SECOND, and unlike the previous two runs, THE PER-METAL DAILY TABLES HAVE NOW CAUGHT UP FOR FOUR OF THE FIVE METALS: copper, nickel, zinc and lead all carry a 03-September row that reproduces the overview to the cent and to the tonne. ONLY THE ALUMINIUM DAILY TABLE STILL ENDS AT 02-SEPTEMBER, which is a publication lag on one page rather than a disagreement about the number - three independent tables and two language versions of the overview all agree that a 03-September session exists and what it settled at. THIRD, every stock line reconciles exactly to the 02-September table value plus the published change: aluminium 246,225 t less 250 t equals 245,975 t; copper 233,850 t plus 800 t equals 234,650 t; nickel 268,848 t plus 1,920 t equals 270,768 t; zinc 100,525 t plus 9,975 t equals 110,500 t; lead 399,600 t less 2,775 t equals 396,825 t. Five out of five to the tonne. FOURTH, and this is the check that matters most today, THE BOARD IS CORROBORATED BY AN INDEPENDENT NON-WESTMETALL SOURCE: Reuters, reporting at 1600 GMT on 03-September, put LME aluminium warehouse stocks at 245,975 tonnes - the same figure, from a different publisher, on the same session. THE AVERAGE COLUMN STILL SHOWS THE COMPLETED AUGUST MEAN, because September contains only three sessions so far. CASH SETTLED $3,303.00, UP $47.50 OR +1.46% ON THE 02-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL, AND THIS IS THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION GAIN THIS PAGE HAS RECORDED SINCE 10-AUGUST. It is also the FIFTH CONSECUTIVE RISING SESSION on the three-month, which Reuters confirms independently, and it took the metal to its highest level in more than three weeks - an intraday $3,328.50, the best print since 12-August. The move cleared the $3,300 handle for the first time since 12-August and lifted September's three-session cash mean to $3,273.17 against a completed August mean of $3,249.63. THE DRIVERS ARE PUBLIC AND THEY ARE PLURAL RATHER THAN SINGULAR, WHICH IS WHY THIS MOVE READS DIFFERENTLY FROM THE 01-SEPTEMBER SPIKE. Reuters attributes it to physical tightness and a softer dollar, and quotes ING's Ewa Manthey saying aluminium is supported by physical market tightness and expectations of firmer seasonal demand in China. The dollar index fell 0.38% on the session, so unlike 02-September - when the currency accounted for essentially the entire move - the currency explains only part of a 1.46% advance. THE INVENTORY NUMBER IS THE HEADLINE FACT OF THIS RUN AND IT IS NOT A WESTMETALL INFERENCE: Reuters states that LME aluminium stocks of 245,975 tonnes are at their LOWEST LEVEL SINCE 1990. That is a thirty-six-year low in exchange-visible metal and it is the single most important piece of new information on this page today.

kpis.label: LME 3-month
kpis.note: THREE-MONTH $3,303.50, UP $50.00 OR +1.54%, AND IT ROSE MORE THAN THE PROMPT DID. That single sentence is the whole of today's curve story and it is the opposite of yesterday's. On 02-September the forward fell further than the prompt and the curve inverted into a $2.00 backwardation; on 03-September the forward rose further than the prompt and the curve fell back through flat into a $0.50 CONTANGO. THE FLAT PRICE AND THE SPREAD MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AGAIN, AND THIS PAGE FLAGS THAT COMBINATION EVERY TIME IT OCCURS - yesterday it flagged a price fall against a tightening curve, today it flags a $47.50 price rally against a LOOSENING curve. The honest reading is that the one-session backwardation did not survive contact with the next session. A prompt tightness signal that reverses within twenty-four hours was positioning, not scarcity, and this page said in advance that persistence was the distinguishing test. It failed the test. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS ALSO REAL AND IS NOT SUPPRESSED: a curve can loosen because the forward is being bought rather than because the prompt is being sold, and on a session when the three-month rose $50.00 to a three-week high, that is the more natural reading. Buying the forward is a bet on the balance in three months; buying the prompt is a bet on metal being unavailable now. Today the market did the first and not the second. Reuters notes analysts still expect the market to remain in deficit this year despite hopes of returning Middle East supply, which is about 9% of global capacity.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: CASH $3,303.00 BELOW THREE-MONTH $3,303.50 IS A CONTANGO OF $0.50. THE CONVENTION IS RESTATED EVERY RUN BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST MISREAD NUMBER IN BASE METALS: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort or carry. The spread has now printed $19.00 contango on 28-August, $0.00 flat on 01-September, $2.00 backwardation on 02-September and $0.50 contango on 03-September. THAT IS A CURVE PINNED ESSENTIALLY AT FLAT, OSCILLATING BY A DOLLAR OR TWO IN EITHER DIRECTION, ON A METAL WHOSE FLAT PRICE MOVED $47.50 IN A SINGLE SESSION. A flat curve on a 1.46% rally is a specific and useful piece of information: it says the rally was expressed in outright length rather than in a scramble for prompt metal. THE TENSION WITH THE INVENTORY NUMBER IS THE MOST INTERESTING THING ON THE PAGE AND IT IS PRESENTED AS A TENSION RATHER THAN RESOLVED. Exchange stock at a thirty-six-year low would normally produce a visible backwardation; aluminium's curve is flat. The two most likely explanations are that a large share of the world's metal sits in off-warrant and unreported inventory that LME stock no longer measures, or that the front is comfortably financed at current rates. Both are plausible, neither is publicly verifiable from free sources, and this page does not choose between them. FOR CONTRAST, LOOK ACROSS THE BOARD: zinc's cash-to-three-month backwardation is $127.50 and copper's is $84.00 on the same session. Those are curves that are pricing genuine prompt scarcity. Aluminium's is not, and that gap is the single best argument for treating the low-stock headline with care.

kpis.label: LME stocks (t)
kpis.note: 245,975 TONNES, DOWN 250 TONNES, AND REUTERS REPORTS THIS AS THE LOWEST LEVEL SINCE 1990. THE THIRTY-SIX-YEAR LOW IS THE HEADLINE AND IT IS INDEPENDENTLY SOURCED, so it is carried at full weight rather than hedged into nothing. IT IS ALSO WORTH SIZING PROPERLY, BECAUSE A LANDMARK AND A SHORTAGE ARE NOT THE SAME THING. The daily change was 250 tonnes, which is 0.10% of the total and roughly two and a half truckloads; the stock has fallen 750 tonnes across the last three sessions and 950 tonnes across the last ten. This is an extremely slow bleed at a very low level, not a drawdown. THE STOCK SERIES HAS FALLEN FROM 264,400 t ON 31-JULY TO 245,975 t NOW, a decline of 18,425 t or 7.0% in five weeks, and from 509,250 t at the start of 2026 - a 51.7% reduction across the year. That trajectory is the substance behind the headline. WHAT THE LOW STOCK DOES NOT DO IS SHOW UP IN THE CURVE, and the honest juxtaposition is that a thirty-six-year inventory low is coexisting with a $0.50 contango. Exchange inventory measures what is on warrant, not what exists; when the on-warrant number reaches a level this low, its information content about physical availability falls rather than rises, because the metal that remains is increasingly the metal nobody wants to move. THE SUPPORTING SERIES IS CHINESE AND IT POINTS THE SAME WAY: SHFE inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 t on 12-June to 391,498 t, and SMM puts Chinese ingot social inventory at 815,000 t as of Thursday, down 22,000 t week on week. Two independent inventory systems are drawing down together, which is a stronger signal than either alone. CHART AXIS: the stock floor of 260,000 was re-bracketed to 235,000 on 04-August and remains correct - the current 245,975 t sits comfortably inside [235,000; 280,000] with 10,975 t of headroom to the floor, which is about forty-four sessions at the current bleed rate.

kpis.label: EUR/USD (LME FX fixing)
kpis.note: THE LME EUR/USD FIXING ROSE TO 1.16140 FROM 1.15780, A GAIN OF 0.31% AND THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION DOLLAR WEAKNESS ON THIS ROW IN A FORTNIGHT. The ECB fixing at 1.16150 and the BFIX reference at 1.16122 corroborate it, so all three published fixings moved together. THIS MATTERS BECAUSE IT SIZES HOW MUCH OF THE ALUMINIUM RALLY WAS CURRENCY AND HOW MUCH WAS METAL, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT MOST OF IT WAS METAL. Cash rose 1.46% in dollars; deflated by the 0.31% move in the fixing, the same settlement rose roughly 1.14% in euro terms. That is the mirror image of 02-September, when a 0.17% dollar decline shrank to 0.04% in euros and the currency explained essentially everything. TODAY THE CURRENCY EXPLAINS ABOUT A FIFTH OF THE MOVE AND THE OTHER FOUR-FIFTHS REQUIRE A REAL EXPLANATION, which is why the inventory headline and the physical-tightness commentary carry weight on this run that they did not carry on the last one. FOR A EUROPEAN CONVERTER THE PRACTICAL POINT IS THAT LANDED COST IN EUROS STILL ROSE SHARPLY - a 1.14% euro-terms increase on top of a duty-unpaid premium that has not moved is a genuine input-cost event, not a translation effect.

lme.commentary: THE 03-SEPTEMBER SESSION IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE 02-SEPTEMBER SESSION AND READING THEM AS A PAIR IS THE ONLY WAY TO GET EITHER RIGHT. Yesterday the flat price fell 0.17% and the curve tightened through flat into a $2.00 backwardation; today the flat price rose 1.46% and the curve loosened back through flat into a $0.50 contango. In both sessions the spread and the price moved in OPPOSITE directions, and this page flags that combination every time because it is the cleanest available separator of a currency or macro move from a physical one. THE FIRST THING TO SETTLE IS THE ONE THIS PAGE PUT ON THE RECORD YESTERDAY. The 02-September backwardation was described here as a small, genuine and easily overstated tightening signal, with an explicit test attached: whether it persisted. IT DID NOT PERSIST. It lasted exactly one session and reversed on the next. That is reported as plainly as the inversion itself was, because a page that advertises a test and then quietly drops it when the answer is inconvenient is not worth reading. A one-session inversion that reverses is positioning, not scarcity. THE SECOND THING IS THAT TODAY'S FLAT-PRICE MOVE IS OF A DIFFERENT QUALITY FROM YESTERDAY'S, AND THE CURRENCY ARITHMETIC IS HOW YOU CAN TELL. On 02-September the dollar index rose 0.18% and the euro-terms decline was 0.04% against a dollar-terms decline of 0.17% - the currency was essentially the whole story. On 03-September the dollar index fell 0.38% and the LME euro fixing rose 0.31%, but the dollar-terms gain was 1.46% and the euro-terms gain was still roughly 1.14%. The currency explains about a fifth. FOUR-FIFTHS OF TODAY'S MOVE REQUIRES A NON-CURRENCY EXPLANATION, WHICH IS WHY THIS RUN TREATS THE INVENTORY EVIDENCE MORE SERIOUSLY THAN THE LAST ONE DID. THE THIRD THING IS THE HEADLINE FACT AND IT IS INDEPENDENTLY SOURCED. Reuters reports that LME aluminium stocks of 245,975 tonnes are at their LOWEST LEVEL SINCE 1990. That is a thirty-six-year low and it is not a Westmetall inference - it is a second publisher, on the same session, quoting the same tonnage. Alongside it, Shanghai exchange inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 tonnes on 12-June to 391,498 tonnes, and SMM reports Chinese ingot social inventory at 815,000 tonnes as of Thursday, down 22,000 tonnes on the week and 37,000 tonnes from the prior Thursday. Two independent inventory systems on two continents are drawing down simultaneously into the Chinese September peak season. That is the strongest form the bull case has taken on this page in weeks. THE FOURTH THING IS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT, AND IT IS SITTING IN PLAIN SIGHT ON THE SAME BOARD. A thirty-six-year inventory low is coexisting with a $0.50 CONTANGO. If prompt aluminium were genuinely scarce, the front would be bid over the forward and it is not. The comparison that makes this concrete is zinc: on the same session, zinc's cash-to-three-month backwardation was $127.50 and it WIDENED even after 9,975 tonnes - a 9.9% single-session build - were delivered into LME warehouses, because exchange data shows ONE ENTITY HOLDS MORE THAN 50% of the zinc warrants and cash contracts. Copper's backwardation is $84.00, having compressed from more than $500 on 17-August. Those are two curves pricing real prompt constraints, one structural and one unwinding. Aluminium's is neither. LOW REGISTERED STOCK AND TIGHT PROMPT METAL ARE RELATED BUT NOT IDENTICAL, and the most likely reconciliation - unverifiable from free public sources and therefore offered as a hypothesis rather than a fact - is that a large and growing share of world aluminium sits off-warrant where LME stock no longer measures it. As the on-warrant number falls, its information content about physical availability falls with it. THE FIFTH THING IS WHAT THE SHAPE OF THE MOVE ACTUALLY SAYS ABOUT WHO WAS BUYING. The three-month rose $50.00 and the cash rose $47.50. Buying concentrated in the forward is a view on the balance in three months; buying concentrated in the prompt is a statement that metal is unavailable now. Today the market did the first. That is consistent with Reuters quoting ING's Ewa Manthey on physical tightness AND expectations of firmer seasonal demand in China - the second half of that sentence is a forward expectation, and the curve says the market is expressing it in the forward. It is also consistent with the deficit consensus Reuters cites for this year surviving the Middle East restart pipeline. THE SIXTH THING IS A GENUINE CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO DATED PUBLIC SOURCES ON THE MACRO, AND IT IS SHOWN RATHER THAN HIDDEN. SMM's 03-September morning summary reports that Jackson Hole sent hawkish signals, that the new Federal Reserve chair's debut remarks leaned hawkish, and that expectations for a SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE have HEATED UP, tightening global liquidity expectations and weighing on aluminium. Reuters, reporting at 1600 GMT the same day, says the LME complex was boosted by a weaker dollar and FADING expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise rates this month. These are irreconcilable and both are public and dated. The tie-breaker available on this page is the price itself: the dollar index fell 0.38% on the session, which is what fading hike expectations look like and is not what heating hike expectations look like. The Reuters read is the later of the two and is corroborated by the currency, so it is given more weight - but the disagreement is disclosed because the SMM piece is the morning-meeting summary and reflects the Asian session, and the two may simply be describing different hours of the same day. THE NET POSITION IS THEREFORE MORE CONSTRUCTIVE THAN IT WAS YESTERDAY AND STILL NOT UNAMBIGUOUS. Five consecutive up sessions, a thirty-six-year inventory low, eleven weeks of Chinese exchange destocking and a move that survives the currency adjustment are a real cluster of evidence. A $0.50 contango, an opening Japanese fourth-quarter premium offer 18-22% below the live record, a Gulf restart running to a published schedule and European capacity firing back up are the other side. Both are on this page.

regional.basis: FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. THIS ROW IS THE Q3-2026 BENCHMARK OF $395/t CIF JAPAN, assessed 06-July-2026 by S&P Global Platts - a record and 12.4% above Q2-2026's $351.50/t. IT IS UNCHANGED AND WILL REMAIN UNCHANGED UNTIL 30-SEPTEMBER, because Q3 is the live quarter and this page does not roll a settled benchmark on the strength of an opening offer in a negotiation that has not concluded. THE Q4-2026 ROUND IS PUBLIC, RUNNING, AND HANDLED SEPARATELY in the settlement-history panel with a null value and a sourced scenario range. THE PUBLIC FACTS ARE UNCHANGED FROM THE PREVIOUS RUN AND NO NEWER DATED REPORT WAS RETRIEVABLE THIS MORNING: Reuters, citing four sources involved in the talks, reported that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 have offered Japanese buyers $310-$325/t for October-December shipments, DOWN 18-22% on the current quarter's record, and that Japanese buyers are targeting BELOW $300 as Asian supply-demand balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes. A source at a Japanese rolling mill is quoted saying the opening offers were closer to realistic levels than in the previous round but still too high given weak spot prices. THE COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE IS LARGE AND IT CUTS AGAINST TODAY'S HEADLINE. On the same page on which LME exchange stock printed a thirty-six-year low, the producers who actually sell physical metal into Asia opened their quarterly negotiation roughly a fifth below the live benchmark. That is the physical market's own verdict on regional availability, and it disagrees with the exchange-inventory headline. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS EQUALLY PHYSICAL AND IS NOT SMALL: aluminium stocks at Japan's three major ports fell to 201,000 t at end-July, the LOWEST SINCE 2010, and Gulf primary output was DOWN 44% YEAR ON YEAR in July per the International Aluminium Institute. A regional premium being negotiated DOWN while regional inventory sits at a sixteen-year low is a genuine contradiction. This page does not resolve it; it notes that the resolution most consistent with both facts is that buyers expect the Middle East restart pipeline to refill the region faster than current stocks would suggest.

FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. CARRIED UNCHANGED AT ITS LAST PUBLIC MARK OF $370/t AND EXPLICITLY NOT RE-ESTIMATED. No newer free, dated public spot assessment on this row's own basis was retrievable this morning. THE ROW'S ANALYTIC VALUE TODAY IS THE SPREAD IT IMPLIES RATHER THAN ITS LEVEL: a $370 spot mark sits $25 BELOW the $395 Q3 contract benchmark, and spot trading below contract is the classic precondition for a lower contract settlement in the following quarter. That is precisely what the Q4 offer range of $310-325 is now doing. The quoted Japanese rolling-mill source in the Reuters report makes the mechanism explicit, saying the opening offers remained too high GIVEN WEAK SPOT PRICES. FOR A PHYSICAL READER THE PRACTICAL POINT IS THAT THE ASIAN REGIONAL PREMIUM CYCLE HAS TURNED, and it turned before the exchange-inventory headline arrived rather than after it - which is a reason to weight the premium signal at least as heavily as the stock signal when reading Asian physical availability.

FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. CARRIED UNCHANGED AT $485/t IN-WAREHOUSE ROTTERDAM DUTY-UNPAID AND EXPLICITLY NOT RE-ESTIMATED; no newer free dated assessment was retrievable this run. THE EUROPEAN ROW IS THE ONE WHERE THE LME MOVE AND THE PREMIUM MOVE COMPOUND RATHER THAN OFFSET, AND TODAY THAT MATTERS. A European buyer pays the LME plus this premium; the LME rose 1.46% in dollars and roughly 1.14% in euros on 03-September, and the premium did not fall to absorb any of it. Landed duty-unpaid cost in Europe therefore rose on the session by essentially the full amount of the metal move. THE STRUCTURAL CONTEXT IS THAT EUROPEAN PREMIUMS HAVE BEEN THE SOFTEST OF THE MAJOR REGIONS THIS YEAR - $485 against a $519.10 Q1-2026 average - and Reuters' report on the Japanese Q4 round cites SOFTER PREMIUMS IN EUROPE as one of the two explicit reasons producers opened lower in Asia, alongside a positive progress report on Middle East production. That is a direct, sourced transmission channel from the European physical market into the Asian benchmark, and it is currently running in the bearish direction.

FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. CARRIED UNCHANGED AT $1,212.50/t DUTY-PAID ROTTERDAM AND EXPLICITLY NOT RE-ESTIMATED. THE VALUE-ADD SPREAD IS WHAT THIS ROW IS FOR AND IT IS UNCHANGED AT ROUGHLY $727.50 over the $485 duty-unpaid ingot premium - the market price of turning an ingot into an extrusion billet in Europe, before duty. THAT SPREAD HAS BEEN REMARKABLY STABLE WHILE THE UNDERLYING METAL HAS MOVED $120 IN FIVE SESSIONS, which is the normal behaviour of a conversion margin and is a useful reminder that downstream European economics are driven by order books and energy, not by the LME. THE READ-ACROSS TO THE PEER PANEL IS DIRECT: the downstream results on this page - Constellium, Kaiser, Novelis - all report on conversion revenue or EBITDA per tonne rather than on metal price, and all three showed expansion in their most recent quarters. A stable billet spread is consistent with that and argues the European conversion market is not the weak link in the chain today; the weak link is primary premium.

FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. CARRIED UNCHANGED AT THE 20-AUGUST PLATTS SEPTEMBER-SHIPMENT MARK OF $2,094/t AND EXPLICITLY NOT RE-ESTIMATED; no newer free dated assessment printed in this window. THE TARIFF-VERSUS-MARKET DECOMPOSITION IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN BECAUSE ITS TARIFF LEG MOVES WITH THE METAL, AND IT MOVED SHARPLY TODAY. At a verified Section 232 rate of 50% on aluminium articles and a cash settlement of $3,303.00, the pure tariff component is 0.50 x $3,303.00 = $1,651.50/t, up from $1,627.75 yesterday - a $23.75 increase driven entirely by the metal rally. Against a $2,094 assessed premium that leaves a residual market component of roughly $442.50/t, DOWN from $466.25 on the previous run. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE POINT AND IT IS UNCOMFORTABLE: because the tariff is levied ad valorem, a rising LME price mechanically inflates the tariff leg and, at a FIXED assessed premium, mechanically SHRINKS the implied market leg. Today's 1.46% metal rally therefore made the US delivered premium look 5.1% less market-driven without a single physical fact changing in the United States. THIS IS A DECOMPOSITION, NOT AN OBSERVATION - no public source splits the US premium into tariff, freight, financing and tightness, and this page does not fabricate one. What it does insist on is that anyone comparing US and non-US premiums adjusts for a $1,651.50 statutory wedge that has nothing to do with physical availability.

FRIDAY 04-SEPTEMBER COMPILE. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY and every row below is carried at its last public assessment date rather than re-estimated to today. NO NEW DATED PUBLIC PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED IN THE 03-SEPTEMBER WINDOW ON ANY OF THESE SIX ROWS, and that is stated rather than papered over with a refreshed-looking date. CARRIED UNCHANGED AT $2,094/t AND EXPLICITLY NOT RE-ESTIMATED; this is the duty-paid row that the tariff decomposition matches against. THE US PREMIUM REMAINS THE MOST TARIFF-INFLATED NUMBER ON THIS PAGE AND THE LEAST INFORMATIVE ABOUT PHYSICAL AVAILABILITY. At today's $3,303.00 cash and a verified 50% Section 232 rate on articles, $1,651.50 of the $2,094 - just under 79% - is statutory rather than commercial. THE COMPARISON THAT MAKES THE DISTORTION VISIBLE: European duty-unpaid is $485 and Japanese Q3 contract is $395, so the US premium is 4.3x Europe's and 5.3x Japan's on the same metal at the same moment. Strip the tariff and the residual $442.50 sits between the two, which is roughly where a large, structurally short, import-dependent market should trade. THE POLICY POSITION IS RE-VERIFIED EVERY RUN AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE and is unchanged: Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085, sets 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives and 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. A reported US-Canada reduction to 25% has been discussed publicly but is NOT in force and is not reflected here.

drivers.text: Q4-2026 producer offers are public and 18-22% below the Q3 record — Top global producers, including Rio Tinto and South32, have offered Japanese buyers $310-$325/t for October-December primary shipments, against the record Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t. Buyers are pushing for BELOW $300 on the argument that Asian balances are easing, in part on rising Indonesian shipments, and a Japanese rolling-mill source is quoted saying the opening offers remain too high given weak spot prices. Reuters names two explicit reasons for the lower opening: a positive progress report on Middle East production, and softer premiums in Europe. THE SIGNIFICANCE THIS RUN IS THE TIMING - this negotiation is running in the same fortnight in which LME exchange stock printed a thirty-six-year low, and the sellers of physical metal are still opening a fifth below the live benchmark.

drivers.text: Japanese port inventory is at a sixteen-year low and Gulf output is down 44% year on year — Aluminium stocks at Japan's three major ports fell to 201,000 t at end-July, the lowest level since 2010, and the International Aluminium Institute reported Gulf primary production down 44% year on year in July. THIS IS THE COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE OFFER RANGE AND IT IS NOT SMALL. A regional benchmark being negotiated 18-22% lower while regional inventory sits at a sixteen-year low is a genuine contradiction, and the reconciliation most consistent with both facts is that Japanese buyers expect the Middle East restart pipeline - EGA now at 315 of 1,262 cells with full pre-war output reaffirmed for Q1-2027 - to refill the region faster than current stocks imply. That is an expectation about the future, not an observation about the present, which is why the premium and the inventory can point in opposite directions at the same time.

drivers.text: The US premium is now roughly 79% statutory tariff, and the metal rally made that worse — At a Section 232 rate of 50% on aluminium articles - re-verified this run against Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026 at 91 FR 34085 - and a 03-September cash settlement of $3,303.00, the pure tariff component of the US delivered premium is 0.50 x $3,303.00 = $1,651.50/t. THE MECHANISM IS WORTH STATING BECAUSE IT IS COUNTERINTUITIVE: because the duty is ad valorem, a rising LME price mechanically inflates the tariff leg and, at a fixed assessed premium, mechanically shrinks the implied market leg. Today's 1.46% metal rally made the US premium look 5.1% less market-driven without a single physical fact changing in the United States. This is a decomposition of published numbers, not a sourced split - no public source breaks the US premium into freight, financing and tightness, and none is invented here.

THE DIRECTIONAL CONTEXT AROUND IT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BEARISH, AND IT IS REPRODUCED RATHER THAN SOFTENED BECAUSE IT MATTERS MORE TODAY THAN IT DID YESTERDAY. SMM's own verdict on the alumina market remains a pattern of STRONG SUPPLY AND WEAK DEMAND: domestic Chinese production continues to recover month on month, Guangxi is steadily ramping with new capacity about to be released and Shanxi resuming, the supply-mismatch logic that supported high ex-China prices has weakened, July net imports fell month on month, PORT INVENTORIES HAVE CLIMBED TO HISTORICAL HIGHS and plant inventories are rising alongside production. SMM concludes supply-side pressure is only increasing, demand shows no bright spots, prices still have downside room and the inventory build is expected to continue. WHY THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT BEARISH ROW ON THE PAGE ON A DAY THE METAL RALLIED 1.46%: cheap alumina is bullish for smelter MARGIN and bearish for metal PRICE, and the distinction is the whole point. Alumina is roughly a third of a smelter's cash cost. When it falls, the marginal tonne of aluminium becomes profitable rather than marginal, and the cost-side mechanism that would otherwise force a curtailment somewhere in the world is removed. A thirty-six-year low in LME exchange stock is a demand-side or logistics-side fact; a collapsing alumina price is a supply-side fact that says nothing shuts. They point in opposite directions and both are on this page. One corroborating public trade remains the 30,000 t done at $379/mt FOB Indonesia on 31-August for October shipment.

THE STRUCTURAL PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE SINGLE LARGEST IDENTIFIABLE UPSIDE RISK TO THE SMELTER COST CURVE. Guinea exported a record 114.8 Mt of bauxite in H1-2026, up 15% year on year, and the government has publicly articulated a target bauxite price above $100 per dry metric tonne against an index in the low seventies - a gap that is the whole motivation for export controls. GUINEA'S APPROACH IS SITE-SPECIFIC EXPORT LIMITS TIED TO FEASIBILITY-STUDY VOLUMES, NOT AN INDONESIA-STYLE OUTRIGHT BAN, and neither the timing nor the final form has been confirmed publicly. THE FLOW DATA CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH SIDES ARE STATED: AL Circle reported global bauxite seaborne flows at 20 Mt in July 2026, up 3% year on year, with shipments to China surging specifically AHEAD of the expected curbs - and cautions in the same piece that July strength may not carry forward for that exact reason. Separately, China's average bauxite import price has fallen roughly 27% from about $88 to about $64 per tonne as Guinean export volumes expanded faster than downstream smelting capacity could absorb them, which has improved smelter economics while squeezing refiner margins. A pre-emptive stock-build ahead of an undefined restriction is fragile support: it pulls demand forward and leaves an air pocket behind it.

alumina.notes: ALUMINA REMAINS A BEAR ARGUMENT ON THIS PAGE AND TODAY IT IS THE SINGLE CLEAREST COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE INVENTORY HEADLINE. No new dated public assessment printed in this window, so all four rows are carried at their stated marks with their ages disclosed. THE ANALYTIC POINT IS UNCHANGED AND WORTH RESTATING PRECISELY BECAUSE THE METAL RALLIED 1.46%: alumina is roughly a third of a smelter's cash cost, and a falling alumina price is BULLISH FOR SMELTER MARGIN AND BEARISH FOR METAL PRICE. It is bearish for the metal because it removes the cost-side mechanism that forces curtailment. In 2022 European smelters shut because power and alumina made the marginal tonne loss-making; in 2026 nothing is loss-making anywhere, which is precisely why Slovalco is firing up after three years, San Ciprian is complete, Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015 and Tomago has been underwritten to 2038. SMM'S OWN LANGUAGE IS STRONG SUPPLY, WEAK DEMAND, PORT INVENTORIES AT HISTORICAL HIGHS AND FURTHER DOWNSIDE ROOM, and roughly 8.6 Mt of new Chinese capacity is scheduled with about 7.6 Mt of it in Guangxi alone. THE CORROBORATION FROM THE PEER PANEL IS DIRECT AND PUBLIC: Nanshan Aluminium International reported H1-2026 alumina sales volume up 15.0% with attributable profit DOWN 74.8%, which is what a volume-up price-down market does to a pure-play refiner, and Chalco's Q2 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year while China Hongqiao's gross profit rose 32.3% on the smelting side. The value is migrating from refining to smelting in public accounts, quarter by quarter. THE HONEST TENSION WITH TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IS THAT A THIRTY-SIX-YEAR LOW IN EXCHANGE STOCK AND A COLLAPSING FEEDSTOCK PRICE ARE BOTH TRUE AT ONCE. The first says metal is scarce where it is measured; the second says nothing will be shut to keep it scarce.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE ROW IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND THE MARKET RE-PRICED IT UPWARD ANYWAY, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF YESTERDAY AND IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE THING ABOUT IT. SMM's 03-September summary carries two dated public statements that frame the position precisely: the US President said a new round of strikes against Iran will not last long and that he is prepared to launch another attack, while Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf said the US must fulfil its relevant commitments BEFORE Iran will act to reopen the Strait. That is a public, explicit, two-sided precondition - the corridor is being held as leverage in a negotiation rather than closed by combat, which makes its reopening a political event with no scheduled date rather than a military one with a foreseeable end. THE CRITICAL DISCIPLINE ON THIS ROW IS UNCHANGED: THE PUBLIC SOURCES DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND THIS PAGE DOES NOT PICK A WINNER. Activist and open-source trackers describe the corridor as effectively closed to commercial shipping; the US Treasury Secretary stated on the record earlier in the week that 17 million barrels of crude crossed on Monday, which is not the throughput of a closed strait. Both are dated, both are public, they are irreconcilable and they are presented as such. WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE is that roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through this waterway - Reuters puts Middle East capacity at about 9% of the global total - and that Gulf primary output was DOWN 44% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY per the International Aluminium Institute. TODAY'S COMMERCIAL LESSON REVERSES YESTERDAY'S AND BOTH ARE KEPT ON THE RECORD: on 02-September the metal gave back part of its Hormuz premium with the story unchanged, and this page called that a positioning phenomenon; on 03-September the metal added 1.46% with the story still unchanged. A risk premium that oscillates while the risk does not is being traded, not underwritten.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: RE-STATED THIS RUN ON A CURRENT PUBLIC BASIS RATHER THAN CARRIED. Traffic through Bab el Mandeb is down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and the US Maritime Administration advisory 2026-006 covering the Red Sea, Bab el Mandeb, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea and Somali Basin REMAINS IN FORCE THROUGH 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Suez transits remain far below pre-crisis normal and carriers are still routing via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. THE DIRECTION FLAG IS DOWN BECAUSE THE CORRIDOR IS DEGRADED, NOT BECAUSE COSTS ARE FALLING - the two Middle East chokepoints on this page are now both impaired simultaneously, Hormuz by live hostilities and Bab el Mandeb by a blockade with a dated advisory attached, and a producer routing Gulf or Red Sea metal to Europe has no unimpaired option. Sources: https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks ; https://gcaptain.com/suez-canal-traffic-stalls-at-60-below-normal-despite-100-days-without-houthi-attacks/

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: STILL NO PUBLIC REPRICE, AND THE ABSENCE IS NOW OLD ENOUGH TO BE A FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. The last public mark this page can cite is 7.5-10% of hull value from 22-July, against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm. Since that mark, at least four merchant vessels have been reported struck in or near the Strait, including two on Monday night and further attacks reported on 01/02-September. HULL-VALUE PREMIUM IS THE FIRST THING THAT REPRICES AFTER TANKERS ARE PHYSICALLY HIT, so the 22-July figure should be treated as a FLOOR and explicitly not as a current quote. This page will not estimate the current level because war-risk rates are negotiated bilaterally and no public assessment exists. THE COMMERCIAL POINT STANDS WITHOUT THE NUMBER: war-risk cost sits inside every regional premium on this page simultaneously and is completely invisible in the LME flat price, which is one reason a falling LME and firm premiums are not the contradiction they appear to be.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: THE BALTIC DRY INDEX REMAINS THE CLEANEST FREELY PUBLISHED PROXY FOR DRY-BULK FREIGHT AND THEREFORE FOR THE BAUXITE AND ALUMINA LEGS OF THE CHAIN, and its trend flag stays DOWN. THE COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERAL: SMM's own cost work attributes the rise in Chinese alumina production costs specifically to imported bauxite CIF, on elevated ocean freight and Guinea rainy-season disruption. Freight is therefore not a background variable in the aluminium cost stack - it is an identified, sourced component of the bauxite delivered cost that feeds the alumina price that forms about a third of smelter cash cost. A SOFTENING DRY-BULK MARKET IS THEREFORE A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DOWNWARD FORCE ON THE GLOBAL COST CURVE alongside falling alumina, and it reinforces the central bear mechanism on this page: nothing is loss-making anywhere, so nothing shuts. THE COUNTERVAILING FORCE IS THE SAME ONE AS ON THE BAUXITE ROW - global bauxite seaborne flows hit 20 Mt in July, up 3% year on year, with China pulling forward ahead of expected Guinean curbs. Pulled-forward tonne-miles support freight now and leave an air pocket behind them.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS 20-AUGUST MARK; no newer public composite print was retrievable this run. Container freight matters less for primary ingot, which moves in bulk and breakbulk, and more for VALUE-ADDED and downstream flows - extrusions, rolled coil, foil, finished components - where a rising box rate is a direct margin cost to fabricators rather than to smelters. It is carried as the downstream half of the freight picture, and it is moving the same way as the dry-bulk half.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: GENERIC COMMERCIAL NOTE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN - BUT WITH A NEW FORWARD-LOOKING POINT WORTH FLAGGING GENERICALLY. Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT $96.965, UP 1.40% AND APPROACHING $97 - A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE RISING SESSION AND THE LARGEST SINGLE-DAY GAIN ON THIS ROW IN A WEEK. Crude is the cleanest live proxy this page has for the Hormuz risk premium, because no traded instrument prices aluminium's chokepoint exposure directly. THE SIGNAL TODAY IS THAT THE ENERGY COMPLEX AND THE METAL MOVED TOGETHER FOR ONCE. On 02-September oil held its gains while aluminium gave part of its own back, and this page read that divergence as evidence the metal's Hormuz premium was positioning rather than conviction. On 03-September both rose - Brent 1.40%, aluminium 1.46% - which is a materially more coherent risk-premium signal than a divergence. THE SECOND-ORDER TRANSMISSION RUNS THROUGH SMELTER POWER AND ALUMINA REFINING RATHER THAN THROUGH SENTIMENT: LNG supply out of the Middle East is the input that took Qatalum to roughly 60% of nameplate and forced Alunorte to half capacity for two days in August. A THIRD CHANNEL IS NOW VISIBLE ON THE INPUT PANEL: green and calcined petroleum coke are refinery by-products, so a sustained crude bid feeds the anode cost line that is already the steepest carbon input on this page.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF EUR 73.20/MWh, DOWN 0.59% AND EASING BACK FROM THE MULTI-YEAR HIGHS OF THE PREVIOUS WEEK. THIS IS THE ONE UNAMBIGUOUSLY HELPFUL NUMBER ON THE MACRO PANEL FOR A SMELTER COST CURVE, AND IT IS THEREFORE UNHELPFUL FOR THE METAL PRICE - the inversion is the same one that runs through the alumina row and it is worth restating. EUROPEAN SMELTING IS THE MARGINAL HIGH-COST TONNE IN THE WESTERN SYSTEM and its power contracts are gas-indexed, so a softening TTF is simultaneously margin relief and one less curtailment catalyst. THE RESTART PIPELINE THIS PAGE TRACKS IS CONCENTRATED IN EXACTLY THE POWER-PRICE-SENSITIVE GEOGRAPHIES A GAS SPIKE WOULD HURT MOST - Slovalco, whose pots are firing after three years offline, San Ciprian, Mt Holly - so gas easing removes the single most plausible mechanism by which that pipeline could stall. UK gilts and eurozone bond yields both recovered on the session on easing energy prices per Trading Economics headlines, which corroborates that the energy leg of the macro softened even as crude rose - a divergence between oil and European gas that is itself a sign the Hormuz premium is being priced in the oil complex rather than the gas complex today.

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY 99.218, DOWN 0.38% - THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION DOLLAR DECLINE ON THIS ROW IN OVER A WEEK AND A DIRECT REVERSAL OF THE PREVIOUS TWO SESSIONS' FIRMNESS. Reuters attributes it explicitly to FADING EXPECTATIONS THAT THE FEDERAL RESERVE WOULD RAISE INTEREST RATES THIS MONTH, and names it as one of two reasons the whole LME complex was bid. THE ARITHMETIC THAT MATTERS FOR ALUMINIUM IS HOW MUCH OF THE 1.46% RALLY THE CURRENCY EXPLAINS, AND THE ANSWER IS ABOUT A FIFTH: the LME EUR/USD fixing rose 0.31%, so in euro terms the same settlement still gained roughly 1.14%. That is the mirror image of 02-September, when a 0.18% dollar rise accounted for essentially the entire 0.17% decline. A MOVE THAT SURVIVES THE CURRENCY ADJUSTMENT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF EVENT FROM ONE THAT DOES NOT, and that distinction is why this run treats the inventory evidence more seriously than the last one did. THE DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN SOURCES IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: SMM's 03-September morning summary reports the opposite - that Jackson Hole was hawkish, that the new Federal Reserve chair's debut remarks leaned hawkish, and that expectations for a SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE have HEATED UP. Both are dated and public. The dollar itself fell 0.38%, which is what fading hike expectations look like, so the Reuters read is given more weight - but the two may simply be describing different hours of the same trading day, and today's US August payrolls will settle it.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD 1.16026, UP 0.12% ON THE LIVE SCREEN, WITH THE OFFICIAL LME FX FIXING PUTTING THE SESSION MOVE LARGER AT 1.16140 FROM 1.15780, A GAIN OF 0.31%. The ECB fixing at 1.16150 and the BFIX reference at 1.16122 corroborate the LME number, so the fixings agree and the live screen simply reflects a later moment. THIS PAGE USES THE LME FIXING FOR ANY SETTLEMENT-BASED CALCULATION because it is struck at the same moment as the metal official; the live rate is carried here for currency context only. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR A EUROPEAN BUYER IS UNAMBIGUOUS AND UNWELCOME: the duty-unpaid Rotterdam premium did not move, so the full metal rally passed into landed cost. Cash rose 1.46% in dollars and roughly 1.14% in euros, and on a $3,303 metal that is about EUR 32/t of additional input cost in a single session, before any premium. FOR A DOLLAR-BASED SELLER THE ARITHMETIC RUNS THE OTHER WAY and the euro strength is worth roughly a third of a percent of realisation on euro-denominated business.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: USD/CNY 6.71968, ESSENTIALLY UNCHANGED AT +0.03% ON A SESSION WHEN THE DOLLAR FELL 0.38% AGAINST ITS BROAD INDEX. THE RENMINBI DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN THE DOLLAR SELL-OFF, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW AND IT MATTERS FOR THE ARBITRAGE. When the dollar falls against the euro but not against the renminbi, the SHFE/LME price ratio moves against Chinese exporters mechanically, without any change in either physical market. SMM'S OWN COMMENTARY FLAGS EXACTLY THIS MECHANISM AND ITS CONSEQUENCE: a recovering SHFE/LME ratio is expected to weaken Chinese export demand as orders on hand are digested. THAT IS A BULLISH DEVELOPMENT FOR THE EX-CHINA BALANCE and one of the few genuine bull arguments on this page that does not depend on the exchange-inventory headline. Chinese exports surged 18.7% in the year to July and have been the principal offset to Middle East supply losses all year; if the ratio keeps recovering, that offset shrinks. THE COUNTERPOINT IS THAT SHFE ITSELF ROSE 0.75% to RMB 24,235/t with a new recent high of 24,290 intraday, so the ratio recovery is being driven by Shanghai strength rather than London weakness - which is a healthier version of the same signal.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: US 10-YEAR 4.787%, ESSENTIALLY FLAT AT +0.3 BASIS POINTS, AND THE STABILITY IS ITSELF THE NEWS AFTER SEVERAL SESSIONS OF A GLOBAL BOND SELL-OFF. Trading Economics headlines UK gilts recovering and eurozone bond yields easing on softer energy prices, so the long end stabilised across three major markets on the same session. THE RELEVANCE TO ALUMINIUM IS INVENTORY FINANCING AND IT IS DIRECT RATHER THAN ATMOSPHERIC. The cost of carrying metal is the funding rate plus warehousing; a high and rising long end makes holding inventory expensive, which pushes metal onto warrant and widens contango, while a stable or falling one does the reverse. THIS IS ONE OF THE TWO CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS FOR THE CENTRAL PUZZLE ON THIS PAGE - why a thirty-six-year low in exchange stock is producing only a $0.50 contango rather than a backwardation. If the front is comfortably financed, metal stays off warrant and the curve stays flat regardless of how low registered stock goes. The alternative explanation is a large and growing off-warrant pool. Neither is verifiable from free public sources and this page does not choose between them. THE NEAR-TERM DRIVER IS TODAY'S US AUGUST PAYROLLS, followed by the 16-September Federal Reserve decision on which two dated public sources currently disagree about direction.

headlines.title: LME ALUMINIUM STOCKS AT 245,975 TONNES ARE AT THEIR LOWEST LEVEL SINCE 1990 - a thirty-six-year low, reported by Reuters at 1600 GMT on 03-September and matching the Westmetall board to the tonne, so the figure is independently corroborated by a second publisher on the same session. The spread and the flat price moved in opposite directions for a second consecutive session, in the opposite configuration. This page attached an explicit persistence test to yesterday's inversion and the inversion failed it. A thirty-six-year inventory low coexisting with a $0.50 contango is the central unresolved contradiction on this page.

ONE ENTITY HOLDS MORE THAN 50% OF LME ZINC WARRANTS AND CASH CONTRACTS, PER EXCHANGE DATA REPORTED BY REUTERS, and zinc's three-month backwardation held at a steep $138 intraday even after 9,975 tonnes were delivered into LME warehouses - a 9.9% single-session inventory build that did not close the spread. On-warrant zinc now stands at 80,225 tonnes. THE ALUMINIUM READ-ACROSS IS BEARISH BY CONTRAST: zinc shows what a curve looks like when prompt metal is genuinely controlled, and aluminium's $0.50 contango on a thirty-six-year inventory low is emphatically not that.

CHINESE INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORY FELL 22,000 TONNES ON THE WEEK TO 815,000 TONNES AS OF THURSDAY, down 37,000 tonnes from the prior Thursday, per SMM - and Reuters separately reports SHFE exchange inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 tonnes on 12-June to 391,498 tonnes. Two independent Chinese inventory systems drawing down together into the September peak season, alongside a thirty-six-year low in LME stock, is the strongest form the bull case has taken on this page in weeks.

SHFE ALUMINIUM CLOSED AT RMB 24,235/t, UP 0.75%, WITH A NEW RECENT HIGH OF RMB 24,290 INTRADAY AND THE PRICE ABOVE ALL FOUR KEY MOVING AVERAGES in a bullish alignment - MA5 24,080, MA10 23,925, MA30 23,820, MA60 23,572. Trading volume expanded to 91,100 lots. SMM notes spot premiums for A00 ingot continuing to rise with morning deals at parity to a RMB 20/t premium, and describes the spot market staging a sharp rebound as tight circulation forced large buyers to raise bids.

Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM OFFERS REMAIN PUBLIC AT $310-325/t, DOWN 18-22% ON THE RECORD Q3 SETTLEMENT OF $395/t, with buyers targeting BELOW $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes. Reuters names two explicit reasons for the lower opening: a positive progress report on Middle East production, and softer premiums in Europe. THE TIMING IS THE POINT THIS RUN - the sellers of physical metal into Asia are opening a fifth below the live benchmark in the same fortnight that exchange stock printed a thirty-six-year low.

JAPANESE PORT INVENTORY IS AT A SIXTEEN-YEAR LOW AND GULF OUTPUT WAS DOWN 44% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY - aluminium stocks at Japan's three major ports fell to 201,000 t at end-July, the lowest since 2010, and the International Aluminium Institute reported Gulf primary production down 44% y/y. A regional benchmark being negotiated 18-22% lower while regional inventory sits at a sixteen-year low is a genuine contradiction, and the reconciliation most consistent with both is that buyers expect the Middle East restart pipeline to refill the region faster than current stocks imply.

EGA HAS 315 OF AL TAWEELAH'S 1,262 REDUCTION CELLS BACK ONLINE - A QUARTER OF THE SMELTER - WITH ALL THREE PRODUCTION LINES RE-ENERGISED BETWEEN MAY AND AUGUST AND FULL PRE-WAR OUTPUT REAFFIRMED FOR Q1-2027. The refinery continues at about 50% capacity and the new recycling plant is ramping to full output by the final quarter of this year, with around 1,000 people involved in the restoration. Reuters puts Middle East capacity at about 9% of the global total and notes analysts still expect a deficit this year despite the returning supply.

SLOVALCO'S SMELTERS ARE FIRING UP AGAIN AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE, moving a line that had sat in the scheduled column for months into the physical column. Combined with San Ciprian complete since 07-April, Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Tomago underwritten by a government support package and a ten-year power agreement to 2038, the Western restart pipeline is now delivering rather than promising - and it is doing so because falling alumina and easing European gas have removed the cost-side trigger that would otherwise force curtailment.

SMM'S ALUMINA READ REMAINS UNAMBIGUOUSLY BEARISH AND REMOVES THE LAST COST-SIDE SUPPORT FOR METAL: strong supply and weak demand, Chinese production recovering month on month, Guangxi ramping with new capacity about to be released and Shanxi resuming, PORT INVENTORIES AT HISTORICAL HIGHS, plant inventories rising, ex-China prices pulled back and further downside room expected. Roughly 8.6 Mt of new Chinese capacity is scheduled with about 7.6 Mt in Guangxi alone. Cheaper alumina is bullish for smelter margin and bearish for metal price, because it means nothing shuts.

A WEAKER DOLLAR LIFTED THE WHOLE LME COMPLEX - DXY 99.218, DOWN 0.38%, WHICH REUTERS ATTRIBUTES TO FADING EXPECTATIONS THAT THE FEDERAL RESERVE WOULD RAISE RATES THIS MONTH. The LME EUR/USD fixing rose 0.31% to 1.16140. BUT THE CURRENCY EXPLAINS ONLY ABOUT A FIFTH OF ALUMINIUM'S MOVE: in euro terms the same settlement still gained roughly 1.14% against 1.46% in dollars, which is the opposite of 02-September when the currency accounted for essentially the entire decline.

TWO DATED PUBLIC SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE DIRECTION OF FEDERAL RESERVE EXPECTATIONS AND THE CONFLICT IS SHOWN RATHER THAN RESOLVED. SMM's 03-September morning summary reports that Jackson Hole sent hawkish signals, that the new Federal Reserve chair's debut remarks leaned hawkish, and that expectations for a SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE have HEATED UP, tightening global liquidity expectations and weighing on aluminium. Reuters at 1600 GMT the same day says expectations of a hike this month were FADING. The dollar fell 0.38%, which favours the Reuters read; today's August payrolls settle it.

COPPER'S SQUEEZE HAS ESSENTIALLY UNWOUND - the cash-over-three-month premium has narrowed to about $68 intraday from MORE THAN $500 ON 17-AUGUST as available stocks have edged higher, with warehouse stock up 800 t to 234,650 t and US July copper imports at a monthly record of around 225,000 tonnes, 46% of it from Chile. A curve that has given back seven-eighths of its squeeze in seventeen sessions is a resolved squeeze. The relevance to aluminium is as a benchmark: that is what a real prompt constraint looks like arriving and leaving, and aluminium has had neither.

IRAN HAS PUBLICLY CONDITIONED REOPENING THE STRAIT ON US COMMITMENTS - Parliament Speaker Qalibaf said the US must fulfil its relevant commitments before Iran will act to reopen the waterway, while the US President said a new round of strikes will not last long and that he is prepared to launch another attack. That makes reopening a political event with no scheduled date rather than a military one with a foreseeable end. Roughly 9% of world primary aluminium supply exits through this corridor and Gulf output was down 44% year on year in July.

SECTION 232 IS RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND ANNEX I-A DERIVATIVES AND 25% ON ANNEX I-B DERIVATIVES, per Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026 published at 91 FR 34085, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. At today's $3,303.00 cash the pure tariff component of the US delivered premium is $1,651.50/t - just under 79% of the assessed $2,094. A reported US-Canada reduction to 25% has been discussed publicly but is NOT in force and is not reflected on this page.

KOREA'S RUSSIAN ALUMINIUM IMPORTS HIT A RECORD 483 kt AS SANCTIONS RISK DEEPENS, per AL Circle, ahead of the EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium that takes effect on 31-December-2026. THE MECHANISM IS REDIRECTION RATHER THAN DESTRUCTION - the tonnes do not disappear, they change destination, which supports European premiums and pressures Asian ones. That is a second, structural reason why the Japanese Q4 offers opened 18-22% below the record while European duty-unpaid has held at $485, and it will persist beyond this negotiation.

THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

status.status: PARTIAL RESTART - 25% OF CELLS (315 of 1,262); REFINERY ~50%; PRE-WAR OUTPUT REAFFIRMED FOR Q1-2027
status.impact: Bearish (supply returning on a dated, published schedule)
status.update: CARRIED AT THE 26-AUGUST-2026 DISCLOSURE AND RE-DATED ONLY, BECAUSE NO NEWER COMPANY STATEMENT PRINTED IN THIS WINDOW. EGA confirmed 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 reduction cells restarted - a quarter of the smelter - after the March Iranian strike on the Khalifa Economic Zone forced an emergency shutdown of all EGA facilities at the site. All three production lines were re-energised between May and August and are being worked simultaneously to speed the recovery, with around 1,000 people involved. Chief Executive Abdulnasser Bin Kalban reiterated the company remains on track to restore FULL PRODUCTION IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 2027. The refinery continues at about 50% capacity and the new recycling plant is increasing output as planned with full output expected by the final quarter of this year; EGA states the pace of further alumina ramp-up will be determined by supply-chain considerations and the optimisation of its alumina sourcing strategy. WHY IT MATTERS TODAY: Al Taweelah is roughly 1.5 Mt/y of nameplate and Reuters puts Middle East capacity at about 9% of the global total, so a restart running to a published schedule is the single largest identified source of returning supply on this panel. It is also the specific fact that Reuters names - a positive progress report on Middle East production - as one of two reasons producers opened the Japanese Q4 premium round 18-22% lower.

A 10-YEAR POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT RUNS TO 2038, starting after the current contract expires on 31-December-2028, with 100% renewable supply from 2033. THE HEADLINE DOLLAR FIGURE IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS PUBLIC SOURCES - A$2.5bn combined versus A$1.76bn or US$1.8bn in other reporting, apparently a scope difference - and Rio Tinto's own release is treated as primary here. The market significance is simple: capacity that the market had a reasonable case for retiring is now committed for another decade.

status.name: Slovalco (Hydro / Penta JV, Slovakia)
status.status: RESTARTING - POTS FIRING UP AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE
status.impact: Bearish (European capacity returning, on a public and now-confirmed schedule)
status.update: NEW ROW ADDED THIS RUN ON A DATED PUBLIC REPORT AND IT MOVES A LINE THAT HAS SAT IN THE 'SCHEDULED' COLUMN FOR MONTHS INTO THE 'HAPPENING' COLUMN. AL Circle reported on 02-SEPTEMBER-2026 that Slovalco's smelters are firing up again after three years offline. The plant was curtailed in 2022 on European power costs and has been carried on this page as a scheduled Q4-2026 resumption of roughly 75 kt; a restart that has physically begun is a materially harder fact than a restart that is planned. THE COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE IS DIRECTIONAL RATHER THAN LARGE: 75 kt is roughly a tenth of one per cent of world primary supply and will not move a balance on its own. WHAT IT DOES DO IS CONFIRM THE PATTERN THAT DOMINATES THE RISK PANEL - idled Western capacity is coming back because prices are high enough and margins wide enough to justify it, which is precisely the self-correcting mechanism that caps a price recovery. THE TENSION WORTH FLAGGING, AND IT IS UNRESOLVED: Slovalco is a gas-and-power-cost casualty restarting into a European gas market that just printed a multi-year high, with TTF up 3.00% on the session. A restart justified by metal prices can be un-justified by power prices, and this page will track whether the ramp holds rather than assuming it does.
src: AL Circle - After three years of being offline, Slovalco's aluminium smelters are firing up again, 02-Sep-2026

status.name: China operators (aggregate, incl. Chalco and Hongqiao)
status.status: AT OR THROUGH THE 45 Mt POLICY CEILING; OUTPUT STABLE, MARGINS WIDE, EXPORTS ELEVATED
status.impact: Mixed (the supply ceiling is real; the margin says nothing shuts)
status.update: THE 45 Mt CAPACITY CEILING SET IN 2017 WAS RENEWED UNDER THE 2025-2027 ACTION PLAN AND OPERATING CAPACITY WAS 44.83 Mtpa AT END-AUGUST, so China is running at or through the policy ceiling with no headroom to add. SMM reports domestic production steady week on week with the liquid-aluminium proportion easing marginally. THE NEW DATED POINTS THIS RUN ARE INVENTORY AND PRICE RATHER THAN OUTPUT, AND BOTH ARE BULLISH. Chinese ingot social inventory fell 22,000 t on the week to 815,000 t and is down 37,000 t from the prior Thursday; SHFE exchange inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 t on 12-June to 391,498 t per Reuters; and the SHFE 2610 contract closed at RMB 24,235/t, up 0.75%, at a new recent high with volume expanding to 91,100 lots. THE OFFSET IS THE EXPORT CHANNEL AND IT IS TURNING BEARISH FOR EX-CHINA BALANCES IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: Chinese exports surged 18.7% in the year to July and have been the principal offset to Middle East supply losses all year, but SMM notes a recovering SHFE/LME ratio is expected to weaken export demand as orders on hand are digested. MARGINS REMAIN THE REASON NOTHING SHUTS: China Hongqiao's H1-2026 gross profit rose 32.3% and Chuangxin's net profit rose 166.1%, both on falling alumina cost. A producer earning that much does not curtail, ceiling or no ceiling.
src: AL Circle - China aluminium nears 46 Mt against the 45 Mt cap; SMM August cost and margin data

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES - VERIFIED; A US-CANADA CUT TO 25% IS REPORTED BUT NOT LAW
status.impact: Mixed (the largest single swing factor in the US delivered premium)
status.update: RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE THIS RUN AND UNCHANGED. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085, sets 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives and 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. A REPORTED US-CANADA REDUCTION TO 25% HAS BEEN DISCUSSED PUBLICLY BUT IS NOT LAW AND IS NOT REFLECTED IN ANY NUMBER ON THIS PAGE. THE ARITHMETIC MOVED TODAY EVEN THOUGH THE POLICY DID NOT, and the mechanism is worth stating because it is counterintuitive: the duty is ad valorem, so at a $3,303.00 cash settlement the pure tariff component of the US delivered premium is 0.50 x $3,303.00 = $1,651.50/t, up $23.75 on the session purely because the metal rallied. Against a fixed assessed premium of $2,094 that leaves an implied market component of about $442.50, DOWN from $466.25 - so a 1.46% metal rally mechanically made the US premium look 5.1% less market-driven without one physical fact changing in the United States. THE COMPARISON THAT SIZES THE DISTORTION: US duty-paid at $2,094 is 4.3x European duty-unpaid at $485 and 5.3x the Japanese Q3 contract at $395 on the same metal at the same moment. Strip the $1,651.50 statutory wedge and the residual sits between the two.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN, AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN A CALENDAR DATE: the Strait of Hormuz de-escalation that this page carried from 26-August - an Iran-Oman announcement of a planned safe maritime corridor - BROKE DOWN OVER THE WEEKEND. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, adjacent to the Strait, on Sunday 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; and the IRGC has claimed that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Reporting on 31-August describes the renewed hostilities as having dashed hopes of near-term normalisation of transit, and Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it while the LME was closed. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT AND IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated that strikes against Iran would be LIMITED and that the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large volumes of oil moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and attributed the Iranian action to sanctions pressure. THE TWO READS ARE NOT RECONCILED HERE BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM EITHER, and no LME session has yet had the opportunity to express a view. SECOND STRUCTURAL POINT, UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE BUT NOW SIMULTANEOUS WITH THE FIRST: Bab el Mandeb transits are down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and US MARAD advisory 2026-006 remains in force through 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Both Middle East chokepoints are impaired at the same time, which leaves a Gulf or Red Sea shipper with no unimpaired routing to Europe and is the physical reason freight is inflating faster than any other cost on this page. THIRD, THE SANCTIONS CLOCK: the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026, and the EU import ban on Russian aluminium takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026 - a dated, certain change to the availability of the metal that dominates LME warrantable stock.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.
src: AL Circle - China eases aluminium shortage after Iran war, but pressure shifts to Western fabricators, 18-Aug-2026

flows.note: RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

~60% of global primary output; the 45 Mt capacity cap is binding at 45.31 Mt/y operating.
