catalysts.text: US NON-FARM PAYROLLS FOR AUGUST - THE SINGLE HIGHEST-WEIGHT INPUT INTO THE 16-SEPTEMBER FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION, AND UNUSUALLY CONSEQUENTIAL THIS MONTH BECAUSE TWO DATED PUBLIC SOURCES CURRENTLY DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH WAY RATE EXPECTATIONS ARE MOVING. Reuters says expectations of a September rise were FADING on 03-September and names that as a driver of the 0.38% dollar decline that lifted the LME complex; SMM's morning summary the same day says post-Jackson Hole signals and a hawkish debut from the new Federal Reserve chair have HEATED UP hike expectations. A hot print vindicates SMM and is dollar-positive and metal-negative; a soft print vindicates Reuters and extends a currency tailwind that was worth about a fifth of yesterday's 1.46% aluminium rally.

WHETHER THE CURVE EVER FOLLOWS THE INVENTORY - THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT OPEN QUESTION ON THIS PAGE. Exchange stock has printed a thirty-six-year low at 245,975 tonnes and the cash-to-three-month spread is a $0.50 CONTANGO; the one-session backwardation of 02-September reversed within twenty-four hours. THE TEST IS EXPLICIT AND IS STATED IN ADVANCE SO IT CANNOT BE QUIETLY DROPPED: a backwardation that appears and PERSISTS for three or more consecutive sessions confirms the low-stock headline is describing real prompt scarcity. A curve that stays pinned within a dollar or two of flat while stock keeps bleeding confirms the opposite - that on-warrant inventory has stopped being a useful proxy for physical availability. Zinc on the same board is the benchmark for what a real one looks like: $127.50 that WIDENED through a 9.9% inventory build.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM NEGOTIATION, PUBLIC AND RUNNING. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 have offered $310-$325/t for October-December against the record Q3 settlement of $395/t; Japanese buyers are targeting below $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes. Talks began the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later this month. THIS IS THE PHYSICAL MARKET'S OWN VERDICT ON ASIAN AVAILABILITY and it will be delivered in the same quarter in which LME exchange stock printed a thirty-six-year low. A settlement near $325 would partially reconcile the two; a print below $300 would say the exchange-inventory headline is not describing the physical market that actually clears metal into Asia.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION. The direction of market-implied probability is currently disputed between two dated public sources, which is why today's payrolls carry more weight than a typical August print. THE TRANSMISSION TO ALUMINIUM IS TWOFOLD. The dollar leg is immediate and was worth about a fifth of the 03-September rally. The funding leg is slower and feeds directly into the inventory-financing question that may be holding aluminium's curve flat despite a thirty-six-year stock low: if the front is comfortably financed, metal stays off warrant and no backwardation develops however low registered stock goes.

FASTMARKETS INTERNATIONAL ALUMINIUM, 40TH EDITION - the industry's principal European gathering and historically a venue at which regional premium expectations for the coming quarter get set in public commentary. IT FALLS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE JAPANESE Q4 NEGOTIATION WINDOW AND IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION. Reuters has already named softer European premiums as one of two explicit reasons producers opened the Asian round 18-22% lower, so European commentary at this event is a sourced input into the Asian benchmark rather than a regional aside.

THE MONTHLY CHINESE PREBAKED ANODE AND COAL-TAR-PITCH SETTLEMENT CYCLE - the next scheduled opportunity for a new dated public mark on the two carbon rows that are currently the steepest upward pressures on the global cost curve. September anodes settled at RMB 5,730/t spot and RMB 5,745/t acceptance, up 1.8% on August, with a large Shandong smelter raising its tender by RMB 100/t month on month; coal tar pitch is up 5.4% in three weeks to RMB 4,960/t. Anodes are 13-16% of cash cost. A second consecutive monthly step up would be the first sustained cost-side support the metal has had in months, at a moment when alumina and European gas are both falling.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - the largest dated structural change on the calendar, and it is already redirecting trade in measurable ways: AL Circle reports Korea's Russian aluminium imports at a record 483 kt as sanctioned metal reroutes to Asia. THE MECHANISM IS REDIRECTION RATHER THAN DESTRUCTION - the tonnes change destination rather than disappearing, which supports European premiums and pressures Asian ones. That is a structural explanation for the direction of the Japanese Q4 offers that does NOT reverse if Hormuz reopens, and it is one more reason registered LME stock is a weaker proxy for physical availability than it used to be.

risks.text: TREND HELD AT UP, AND THE RESTART PIPELINE PICKED UP A RE-CONFIRMED SCHEDULE RATHER THAN A NEW ASSET THIS RUN. EGA's own disclosure has 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 reduction cells back online - a quarter of a roughly 1.5 Mt/y smelter - with all three production lines re-energised between May and August, around 1,000 people on the restoration, and the chief executive reiterating full pre-war production in the FIRST QUARTER OF 2027. Slovalco's pots are firing after three years offline, San Ciprian completed on 07-April, Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Tomago is underwritten by a government package and a ten-year power agreement to 2038. WHY THIS ROW STAYS RED ON A DAY THE PRICE ROSE 1.46%: Reuters explicitly names a positive progress report on Middle East production as one of two reasons producers opened the Japanese Q4 premium round 18-22% below the record. The restart pipeline is not a forecast this page is making - it is a sourced input into a live commercial negotiation, and the buyers on the other side of that negotiation are pricing it. The offsetting fact is stated too: Reuters reports analysts still expect the market to remain in deficit this year DESPITE the returning Middle East supply. || TREND HELD AT UP AND REINFORCED BY TWO DATED ITEMS IN THE LAST 24 HOURS. FIRST, SLOVALCO'S SMELTERS ARE PHYSICALLY FIRING UP AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE per AL Circle on 02-September - roughly 75 kt moving from this page's 'scheduled' column into its 'happening' column, which is a materially harder fact than a plan. SECOND, AND MORE TELLING, THE PRODUCERS THEMSELVES CITED SUPPLY RELIEF AS THE REASON THEY CUT THEIR OWN PRICES: Reuters reports Q4-2026 Japanese premium offers of $310-325/t, down 18-22% on the $395 record, with the stated causes being a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer European premiums. When the sell side voluntarily opens 20% lower and names restart progress as the reason, that is the supply-relief risk being confirmed by the parties with the most information and the least incentive to confirm it.

TREND CUT FROM FLAT TO DOWN - THE RISK THAT THE STOCK DRAW HAD STOPPED IS NOW CLEARLY RECEDING, AND THE EVIDENCE IS NO LONGER A SINGLE SESSION. Warehouse stock fell 250 t to 245,975 t on 03-September, the THIRD CONSECUTIVE DRAW, taking 750 t out across three sessions and 950 t across ten after a thirteen-session period in which only 200 t moved. More importantly, REUTERS REPORTS 245,975 TONNES AS THE LOWEST LEVEL SINCE 1990 - a thirty-six-year low, independently corroborated by a second publisher quoting the same tonnage on the same session. THE CORROBORATION FROM CHINA IS STRONGER STILL AND IS WHAT JUSTIFIES CUTTING THE TREND RATHER THAN HOLDING IT FLAT: SHFE inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 t on 12-June to 391,498 t, and Chinese ingot social inventory fell 22,000 t on the week to 815,000 t, down 37,000 t from the prior Thursday. Three inventory series on two continents drawing simultaneously is a materially different piece of evidence from one 500-tonne session. THE DISCIPLINE THAT STAYS ATTACHED: the daily move is still only 0.10% of the stock, and the curve has not confirmed any of it. || TREND CUT FROM UP TO FLAT - THE FLATLINE BROKE, BY THE SMALLEST MEANINGFUL AMOUNT THE EXCHANGE REPORTS, AND THAT IS WORTH EXACTLY WHAT IT IS WORTH AND NO MORE. Warehouse stock fell 500 t to 246,225 t on 02-September after printing 246,725 t for three consecutive sessions and moving 200 t across the thirteen sessions from 17-August; today's single move exceeds that whole thirteen-session total. IT IS ALSO 0.20% OF THE STOCK AND ROUGHLY TWO HOURS OF WORLD PRIMARY OUTPUT, and lead - a metal with no supply story whatsoever - drew 5,075 t on the same board, ten times as much. THE TREND IS SET TO FLAT RATHER THAN DOWN DELIBERATELY: the risk that the draw has stopped is no longer worsening, because it demonstrably resumed, but a single 500-tonne session is not enough evidence to call it improving. What makes it worth anything at all is that it coincided with the curve inverting - the first session in this cycle on which inventory and structure pointed the same way at the same time.

TREND CUT FROM UP TO DOWN - THE MARKET PAID FOR THE GULF DISRUPTION AGAIN, AND THIS TIME IT PAID WHILE THE ENERGY COMPLEX PAID TOO. This risk is the risk that the market STOPS PAYING for the Gulf disruption, not the risk of the disruption itself, and it was raised back to UP yesterday because aluminium finished third of five on 02-September while Brent and European gas both rose. ON 03-SEPTEMBER THE DIVERGENCE CLOSED: aluminium led the entire board at +1.46% against copper +0.03%, nickel +0.51%, zinc -0.11% and lead -0.16%, and Brent rose 1.40% to $96.965 on the same session. THE METAL AND THE ENERGY COMPLEX MOVED TOGETHER, which is a materially more coherent risk-premium signal than a divergence, and it is why the trend is cut. THE UNDERLYING STORY ALSO HARDENED RATHER THAN SOFTENED: Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf said publicly that the US must fulfil its relevant commitments BEFORE Iran will act to reopen the Strait, while the US President said a new round of strikes will not last long and that he is prepared to launch another attack. A corridor held as explicit negotiating leverage has no scheduled reopening. THE CAUTION THAT REMAINS: this row has now flipped three times in four sessions, which is itself evidence that the premium is being traded rather than underwritten. || TREND RAISED BACK FROM DOWN TO UP AFTER ONE SESSION, AND THE REVERSAL IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN QUIETLY MADE. This risk is the risk that the market STOPS PAYING for the Gulf disruption, not the risk of the disruption itself. It was cut to DOWN yesterday because aluminium led the entire LME board on 01-September while copper and nickel fell on the same hostile macro. ON 02-SEPTEMBER THAT LEADERSHIP DID NOT REPEAT: aluminium finished THIRD OF FIVE at -0.17%, behind nickel at +1.10%, while the underlying story got WORSE rather than better - further tanker attacks were reported in the Strait on 01/02-September including an Iranian strike on a Saudi tanker reported to have killed two Filipino sailors, Brent rose a fourth consecutive session to $95.117 and European gas rose 3.00% to a 2023 high. THE ENERGY COMPLEX KEPT PAYING AND THE METAL DID NOT. A risk premium that decays while its cause persists is a positioning phenomenon, and positioning unwinds faster than shortages do - which is precisely the risk this row exists to track.

TREND HELD AT DOWN AND THE HARD INVENTORY SERIES KEEPS GETTING BETTER. SMM reports Chinese ingot social inventory fell 22,000 t week on week to 815,000 t as of Thursday, down 37,000 t from the prior Thursday, and describes the September peak season as providing strong support below aluminium prices. SHFE exchange inventories have now fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 t on 12-June to 391,498 t per Reuters. THE PRICE CONFIRMS THE INVENTORY: the SHFE 2610 contract closed at RMB 24,235/t, up 0.75%, at a new recent high of RMB 24,290 intraday, above all four key moving averages in bullish alignment with volume expanding to 91,100 lots, and SMM reports spot premiums for A00 ingot rising with large buyers raising bids as circulation tightened. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS THE ONE SMM ITSELF MAKES: downstream operating rates remain under pressure, the pre-peak-season stockpiling that was expected did not fully materialise, and the transition from off-season to peak season is not yet clearly established. This is a destocking story, not yet a consumption story. || TREND HELD AT DOWN, AND THE HARD INVENTORY SERIES REMAINS THE REASON. Chinese ingot social inventory finished August at 850,000 t, in line with expectations, on a counter-seasonal destock SMM expects to continue into September; SHFE aluminium 2610 closed HIGHER on 02-September at RMB 24,100/t on a session London closed lower, with USD/CNY essentially unchanged so the divergence is not an FX artefact. SMM credits the September peak season explicitly. THE HONEST BEARISH OFFSET INSIDE THE SAME SOURCE IS NOT SUPPRESSED: SMM also notes the recovering SHFE/LME ratio is expected to WEAKEN Chinese export demand as orders on hand are digested, which reduces the export flow that has been partially offsetting the Gulf shortfall. Chinese exports rose 18.7% year on year in the twelve months to July, so that flow is large enough for its reduction to matter.

TREND CUT FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE TWO BEST PUBLIC SOURCES NOW DISAGREE ABOUT THE DIRECTION OF RATE EXPECTATIONS - WHICH IS ITSELF A REASON NOT TO CARRY A DIRECTIONAL TREND. Reuters, at 1600 GMT on 03-September, attributes the 0.38% fall in the dollar index to FADING expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise rates this month, and names it as one of two reasons the whole LME complex was bid. SMM's morning summary the same day reports the opposite: post-Jackson Hole hawkish signals, a hawkish debut from the new Federal Reserve chair, and expectations for a September HIKE that have HEATED UP, tightening global liquidity expectations. Both are dated and public and this page shows the conflict rather than resolving it by preference. THE LONG END STABILISED ALONGSIDE, WHICH SUPPORTS FLAT RATHER THAN UP: the US 10-year was essentially unchanged at 4.787%, and Trading Economics headlines UK gilts recovering and eurozone yields easing on softer energy prices. THE MECHANISM THIS ROW TRACKS REMAINS INVENTORY FINANCING AND IT IS NOW CENTRAL TO THE PAGE'S MAIN PUZZLE: if the front is comfortably financed, metal stays off warrant and the curve stays flat no matter how low registered stock goes - which is one of the two candidate explanations for a $0.50 contango on a thirty-six-year inventory low. TODAY'S US AUGUST PAYROLLS SETTLE THE DISAGREEMENT. || HELD AT UP AND THE MECHANISM SHARPENED TODAY IN A WAY THAT IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN ATMOSPHERIC. The global bond selloff extended - US 10-year 4.817%, UK 5.283%, the 10-year JGB through 3% at 3.018%, Australia 5.225%, and the GERMAN 10-YEAR AT 3.3884%, FLAGGED AS A FRESH 15-YEAR HIGH - with roughly a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point US rate HIKE priced for 16-September. WHY IT BITES HARDER NOW THAT THE CURVE HAS INVERTED: a backwardation means holders are PAID to lend metal to the prompt rather than paying to carry it, and $2.00 of backwardation against a 4.8% funding rate does not come close to compensating a carry. Rising funding costs and an inverted curve push the rational holder the SAME way - toward delivering metal into the front. That is the mechanism by which a backwardation resolves itself rather than persisting, and it is why today's curve signal should not be extrapolated.

HELD AT UP, BUT THE COMPOSITION CHANGED AND THE ENERGY LEG REVERSED. THE RELIEF IS REAL AND IS STATED FIRST: European gas TTF fell 0.59% to EUR 73.20/MWh, easing back from the multi-year highs of the previous week, and Trading Economics headlines UK gilts and eurozone yields recovering on softer energy. Gas-indexed European power is the marginal high-cost tonne in the Western system, so this is margin relief - and, unhelpfully for the metal, it is also one less curtailment catalyst on exactly the restart pipeline in the first risk row. THE CARBON CHAIN IS WHY THE TREND STAYS UP RATHER THAN MOVING TO FLAT: coal tar pitch is up 5.4% in three weeks to RMB 4,960/t, prebaked anodes stepped up 1.8% to RMB 5,730/t for September with a large Shandong smelter raising its tender by RMB 100/t month on month, and silicon is up 8.7% in six weeks to RMB 9,400/t - the steepest trend anywhere on the input panel and a direct casthouse cost. Anodes are 13-16% of cash cost. THE HONEST ADMISSION REPEATS FROM THE LAST RUN: no new dated SMM fluoride-salt, silicon or magnesium print inside this window was freely retrievable, the anode and pitch monthly settlement cycle publishes around the 17th-18th, and nothing was appended or estimated. Three rows carry permanently empty histories because no public series exists - smelter power, cathode blocks and Ti-B grain refiner - and smelter power is 30-40% of cash cost, so the largest line in the stack is invisible to any public-only analysis including this one. || HELD AT UP WITH ONE NEW DATED POINT AND ONE HONEST ADMISSION. THE NEW POINT IS ENERGY: European gas TTF rose 3.00% to a 2023 high on Strait-related supply news, with UK gas doing the same and Brent up a fourth session at $95.117. Gas-indexed European power is the marginal high-cost tonne in the Western system, so this is simultaneously a cost input and a curtailment risk on exactly the restart pipeline listed in the first risk row - Slovalco is a 2022 power-cost casualty restarting into a multi-year gas high. THE ADMISSION IS THAT THE REST OF THE BASKET HAD NO NEW MARKS: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke are on monthly settlement cycles publishing around the 17th-18th, and no newer free dated SMM fluoride-salt, silicon or magnesium print was retrievable this morning.
